description: hron conformance test suite. All eval tests use now=2026-02-06T12:00:00+00:00[UTC] (Friday) unless overridden per-test.

_eval_assertion_types.next: Full timestamp of the next occurrence from now. null means no future occurrence exists.
_eval_assertion_types.next_date: Date-only (YYYY-MM-DD) of the next occurrence. Implementations should call next_from(now) and compare only the date component.
_eval_assertion_types.next_n: Array of full timestamps for N consecutive occurrences. N defaults to the array length; if next_n_count is provided, request that many and compare the returned array.
_eval_assertion_types.next_n_count: How many occurrences to request from next_n_from(). Defaults to next_n array length if omitted.
_eval_assertion_types.next_n_length: Expected number of results when exact timestamps are not specified (use instead of next_n when only the count matters).
_eval_assertion_types.matches: Boolean: does the expression match the given datetime? Tests are in eval.matches section with 'datetime' and 'expected' fields.

_behavioral_notes.time_boundary: next_from uses strict greater-than (>). If now equals an occurrence time exactly, that occurrence is skipped.
_behavioral_notes.week_repeat_default_anchor: When no 'starting' clause is given, week_repeat uses epoch Monday (1970-01-05) as the anchor for computing week parity.
_behavioral_notes.day_skip: If a month doesn't have the requested day (e.g., Feb 30), that month is skipped entirely.
_behavioral_notes.named_date_recurrence: Named exceptions (e.g., 'except dec 25') recur every year. ISO exceptions (e.g., 'except 2026-12-25') apply to that one date only.
_behavioral_notes.cron_limitations: from_cron supports standard 5-field cron including ranges, steps, L (last day), W (nearest weekday), # (nth weekday), @ shortcuts, and named months/days. Directional nearest weekday (next/previous) is hron-only and cannot be converted to cron.
_behavioral_notes.interval_anchor: For day/month/year/ordinal intervals > 1, alignment is computed from the anchor date. Default anchor is epoch (1970-01-01). The 'starting' clause overrides it. Formula: (date_offset - anchor_offset) mod interval == 0.
_behavioral_notes.contradictory_schedules: Schedules with mutually exclusive constraints (e.g., 'until' before 'starting', impossible day-of-month + 'during' filter) are syntactically valid and must parse successfully. Evaluation returns empty results (no occurrences). Implementations must not error or loop infinitely.

invariants.description: Self-consistency checks with no expected values. For each test, parse the expression, evaluate it at 'now', and check that the library's answers agree with each other under every rule; timestamps are equal when they are the same instant.

rules.next_matches: If nextFrom(now) returns t, then matches(t) is true.
rules.next_after_now: If nextFrom(now) returns t, then t is strictly after now.
rules.next_n_chain: nextNFrom(now, count) is strictly increasing, is empty exactly when nextFrom(now) is null, starts with nextFrom(now), and each later element equals nextFrom(the element before it).
rules.occurrences_prefix: Taking count elements from occurrences(now) gives exactly nextNFrom(now, count).
rules.between_window: If nextNFrom(now, count) is non-empty and its last element is L, then between(now, L) equals nextNFrom(now, count).
rules.prev_inverse: For consecutive elements a, b of nextNFrom(now, count), previousFrom(b) equals a.
rules.prev_before_now: If previousFrom(now) returns p, then p is strictly before now, matches(p) is true, and nextFrom(p) is null or not earlier than now.
